# 4 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Fraternal Love and Unity

---

**1** Were I to praise the endurance of those young men, that praise would be inadequate to their achievement. For they despised the passions and conquered their torments.

**2** How can I adequately praise also the magnanimity of the brothers, and their noble obedience to the law?

**3** Just as the branches of a tree, though each grows in its own direction, are nevertheless one at the root, so too these brothers were one in their devotion to the law.

**4** Having been formed in the same law and trained in the same virtues, they were bound together in love.

**5** Their shared nature deepened their love, and the law strengthened it, and righteousness made it firm.

**6** The brothers' harmony confirmed their courage, so that the tyrant was powerless to divide them from one another.

**7** The eldest encouraged the others, saying: Be courageous and noble, brothers.

**8** Remember that it was by the same God who created us that the law was given, and that our father Jacob lived by it and proved its truth in his own life.

**9** And the Almighty will not abandon us who do not turn aside from the commandments of our fathers.

**10** The second said: Be courageous, brothers! For we are sons of Abraham and we will not be put to shame in any regard.

**11** The third said to the others: Be courageous and noble, brothers, for we are fighting the battle of righteousness.

**12** The fourth said: Brothers, do not fear the one who kills the body but cannot destroy the soul.

**13** The fifth said: Brothers, this present time is brief and our life is passing away, but the name of those who die for virtue endures forever.

**14** The sixth said: Do not be overcome by grief, brothers, for death is a release from the sufferings of this present age.

**15** And the seventh, the youngest of all, said: Do not be afraid, brothers; but take courage, for it would not be worthy of those who are ripe in wisdom to be afraid of a man who can only kill the body.

**16** Then each of them, trusting in this reasoning, entered into the flames of torture with full confidence that he would never cease to live.

**17** How marvelous! What praise these noble souls deserve, who having mastered their passions and overcome the fear of death went willingly to the altar of holy martyrdom!

**18** Did not the mother herself make this brave choice — she who chose the better death for her sons and thereby sealed their immortal victory?

**19** Is it not worthy of the highest praise that she endured the death of seven sons in a single day and did not allow her spirit to be broken?

**20** For from her womb they came, and in her womb they were nurtured, and by her teaching and her love they were raised to the endurance of virtue — and in her heart she held them even as they died.
